sketch:
Observe: split view. Top-left: modulating signal m(t) (sinusoid,
sliders for f_m, amplitude); top-right: carrier p(t) (sliders for
f_p ≫ f_m). Bottom-left: AM output s(t) = (1 + k·m(t))·cos(2πf_p t)
with envelope highlighted. Bottom-right: spectrum showing carrier
line at f_p flanked by two sidebands at f_p ± f_m. Sliders for
modulation depth m. Experiment: hit a target time-domain envelope
or a target spectrum. Evaluate: given only the spectrum, deduce
f_p, f_m, m. Wrinkle: over-modulation (m > 1) inverts the envelope
— visible catastrophe teaches why we keep m ≤ 1.
